method: Five independent AI panels; Borda 5/4/3/2/1 within each topic; complete coverage required. Not human user testing.

jurors.lens: Engineering semantics and evidential honesty: preserve identities, conditional state, explicit assumptions, provenance, and the boundary between a generated candidate and a human decision.
jurors.evidence: Independently inspected JURY.md, the complete manifest, all four topic briefs, all 20 rationales, and all 20 SVG/CSS modules across phases 0 through 4 and their choice branches. Viewed all 20 supplied Chrome Explore stills and all four complete topic contact sheets. Read verification.json reporting 20 submissions and 10 or 15 deterministic renders per entry. Static composition is observed; choreography scores assess authored CSS timing and geometry, not animation personally watched. Alternate states and other phases were inspected in source. No mobile-device, Korean-layout, assistive-technology, or human-comprehension acceptance is claimed. Small-format concerns are inferred from fixed SVG text sizes and scaled contact sheets.

jurors.lens: Motion choreography and causal storytelling: whether ordered reveals explain a dependency, whether identity and the selected state survive all five phases, and whether a stopped process actually stays stopped.
jurors.evidence: Independently inspected the manifest, topic briefs, jury and production contracts, all 20 rationale files, and the SVG/render-state/CSS source for all five phases and every supplied interaction choice. Visually inspected all 20 host-produced Chrome entry screenshots and the four topic contact sheets. These are static phase-2 default-choice images; the other phases and alternate choices were evaluated from source, not personally observed in a browser. All animation judgments are inferred from authored CSS, timing, geometry and class assignments; I did not watch animation. Read motion-lab/verification.json: 20 submissions, zero missing, 225 phase/choice renders, with per-entry size and translation metrics. Those checks do not establish semantic correctness, collision freedom or mobile usability. Small-label concerns are inferred from the contact sheets and SVG font sizes, not a physical-device test. No other juror ballot was read.

jurors.lens: Visual composition and art direction: a distinctive silhouette, disciplined hierarchy, meaningful spatial metaphor and an intelligible five-phase visual argument, scored against the fixed semantic, distinction, choreography and usability maxima.
jurors.evidence: Independently read JURY.md, manifest.json, the equal-production contract, all four topic briefs, all 20 entry.js modules and rationale.json files, including their five phase branches and choice handling. Visually inspected all 20 supplied individual Chrome captures and all four topic contact sheets. Those captures show static phase-2 compositions in the base, equipment or missing-evidence state; alternate choices and other phases were assessed from SVG construction and source, not claimed as visually observed. Choreography scores assess authored CSS keyframes, timing, sequencing and semantic intent; I did not watch animation or operate a browser. Read verification.json: 20 of 20 entries, no missing entries, 225 phase/choice renders in total, each module below 32 KB. These structural metrics do not establish visual or device acceptance. At 350 px width, a 16-unit label in a 720-unit SVG is approximately 7.8 px; small secondary labels remain a source-inferred mobile concern across the field. No other juror ballot was read.

jurors.lens: Interaction consistency, accessible state communication, and readability when a 720-unit SVG is reduced to a small screen. Fixed rubric: semantic fidelity 35, visual distinction 25, choreography 20, readability/usability 20.
jurors.evidence: Independently inspected JURY.md, manifest.json, CONTRACT.md, all four topic briefs, all twenty rationales and entry modules, four supplied Chrome contact sheets, and every individual entry screenshot. The observed screenshots show desktop English explore/default states, not every visual phase or alternative. Inspected all five authored phases and all condition branches in source and independently rendered all 225 phase/choice combinations in Node, including checking whether accessible descriptions change with choices. Read verification.json. The supplied 200 desktop English/Korean text-bound checks are supporting evidence of bounds only. Motion judgments are inferred from CSS durations, keyframes and state geometry; I did not watch animation. Small-screen judgments are inferred from the fixed viewBox, nested scales, label sizes and visual density; no mobile, touch, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion browser acceptance is claimed. At a 350px SVG width, 16/18/20-unit text becomes approximately 7.8/8.8/9.7px before any inner scaling, so the nominal minimum font rule is not a readability guarantee. No other ballot was read.

jurors.lens: Cross-topic visual identity and coherent synthesis: each subject should have its own recognizable silhouette, semantic action and motion logic, within shared typography and controls. Scores use semantic 35, distinction 25, choreography 20 and usability 20; choreography is judged from authored source, not watched animation.
jurors.evidence: Read JURY.md, manifest.json, the equal production contract, all four topic briefs, all twenty rationale.json files and the twenty entry modules through their SVG/CSS, phase implementations and choice logic. Inspected actual Chrome still contact sheets for pid, calc, ontology and tbe, plus larger individual stills for P2, P3, C2, O5 and T5. Executed source render functions to inspect phase/choice text for the calc, ontology and tbe modules. The observed screenshots show the desktop English explore state with the default choice; other phases, alternate choices and finite motion behavior are source-inferred. Read verification.json reporting 20 submissions and 10 or 15 renders per module. The organizer separately reports 200 desktop EN/KO default-state outer-bound checks without overflow; that does not establish internal label spacing, mobile readability or animation acceptance. No browser animation, physical device, human-user research or other juror ballot was inspected.

jury_contributions.comment: Use retained translucent originals, conditional working proof and the explicit no-final-judgment language; keep annotation motion clearly illustrative.
Use separate retained-original and working-draft layers, conditional proof wording and a filing action. Keep the large editorial spacing but avoid copying the entire palimpsest layout.

Use translucent retained-original/proof separation, serif hierarchy and local editorial marks. Add a real comparison connection so the sheets explain the technical-review relation rather than only document handling.

Use the preserved original, separate annotated working layer and clear rationale/applicability question. Keep essential text unobscured and increase contrast of thin source annotations at small widths.
Reuse retained original versus working proof, large editorial type and local annotation; omit repeated full-page stacking so source identity remains readable.

entries.contribution: Reworked retained-original and working-proof separation into a spacious, independently labeled comparison spread and then a common archival jacket. Local editorial brackets expose the proposed question and its rationale without suggesting that a human has already reviewed them. Repeated stacked-sheet compositions and a decorative pencil are omitted.

jury_contributions.comment: Use the physically empty reference position and the conditional action ribbon; keep source text large and remove lens detail that does not reveal information.
Use a physically empty evidence footprint that changes the next action and persists into review/outcome. Reject a decorative magnifier unless it reveals additional relevant clause content.
Use the physically vacant evidence footprint, large next action and source-linked filing logic. Remove unnecessary magnifier reflections and peripheral desk props.
Use the empty evidence footprint, named next action and downstream conditional clarification. Simplify the lens and render the action as plain output status unless it is an actual control.

Reuse the physically vacant evidence position and original/change/rationale jacket; retain the missing/linked branch through the complete story and use the magnifier only when it reveals a specific clause relation.

entries.contribution: Reworked the physically vacant evidence leaf into a compact footprint that is consistently missing or linked in every phase. Its conditional filing logic survives, while the decorative magnifier, paper clips and button-like action ribbon are omitted. Actions are plain output labels or an attached clarification fold.

jury_contributions.comment: Use a single aligned requirement/reply/evidence lane and its review-band timing; avoid a full placeholder matrix when only one clause is being explained.
Use the clause-aligned scan across requirement, reply and evidence. Reveal the next action only after the scan reaches that clause; reduce the matrix to one meaningful example for small screens.

Use the illuminated cross-source clause alignment and stable requirement/reply/evidence positions. Reduce the matrix to one large active comparison so it remains an illustration rather than a miniature table UI.
Use requirement/reply/evidence alignment and the active-clause review band. On phones replace the full matrix with one vertically aligned clause; remove checkbox-like decorative evidence marks.
Reuse horizontal requirement-to-reply-to-evidence alignment and a single purposeful review band; replace the miniature three-row table with one enlarged active clause plus a small context index.

entries.contribution: Reworked requirement/reply/evidence alignment into one enlarged concertina record, with three vertically aligned document roles for one clause. A single scanning bracket reaches the evidence row before the final alignment label appears. The three-row miniature matrix and checkbox-like placeholders are rejected.

jury_contributions.comment: Use the unmistakable output-held interlock and separate clarification fold; reject unconditional DRAFT scenes and propagate the evidence state throughout.
Use the physical unsupported-output interlock and explicit clarification branch. Reject unconditional draft scenes and roller motion that suggests successful processing while output is held.

Use the understandable physical output interlock and a restrained cobalt accent. Reject the complete face-like press, unconditional roller activity and especially the draft shown after the missing-evidence choice.

Use the visible output interlock and strong held-versus-draft distinction. Reject the unconditional later DRAFT scenes; missing evidence must remain a clarification in every phase and accessible description.

Reuse the output interlock and draft-only marking as a small paper-feed mechanism; reject unconditional draft output in later missing-evidence phases and avoid decorative rollers when no document action is occurring.

entries.contribution: Reworked the output-held principle as two striped interlock jaws embedded in the paper channel, with a separate side clarification. There is no face-like press or decorative roller. The missing branch never gains a visible draft in review or outcome; only the linked branch receives an outlined review artifact.

jury_synthesis.proposal: Start with the exact requirement and reply on retained paper, align one clause with its evidence slot, then move that clause through separate source-linkage and human-applicability checkpoints. Missing evidence must stop at clarification in every later phase; linked evidence may create only a review draft. Retain original, change and rationale in a translucent archive. Combine an empty evidence footprint, an explicit mechanical stop and a human review mark, with corrected baton clearance and no automated approval implication.

Build a new clause-alignment folio: retain requirement and vendor reply on two fixed source rails, with an evidence slot aligned to the same clause. A review bracket crosses those rails once, then the clause carrier reaches a physical support gate. Missing evidence stops the carrier before the gate and unfolds an attached clarification; linked evidence attaches a source slip, opens only that gate, and reveals a separate translucent draft layer. The human checkpoint stays visibly unresolved. Review exposes original, change and rationale together; outcome files either clarification or draft beside the unchanged source. Combine T2's alignment, T1's real vacancy, T3's interlock logic, T4's preserved layers and T5's timed checkpoints in new folio geometry. Never let later phases silently turn the missing branch into a draft.

Create a new Clause proofing relay: two large retained source leaves first align on one illuminated clause band. That clause becomes a readable excerpt carried across an explicit evidence footprint toward a separate human-review boundary. Missing evidence closes a simple mechanical interlock and produces a clarification; linked evidence opens only that first boundary and yields a draft that still stops for applicability review. A translucent proof overlay records the exact change and rationale, then files alongside the original. Borrow the press principle without the complete machine, and use a single clause comparison instead of a full matrix. This is a newly composed documentary relay, not a selected winner; state continuity, bilingual small-screen layout and actual pause choreography must still be verified.

Build a new clause review folio whose central element is the requirement/reply pair and its evidence slot. The selected clause has two compact checkpoints below it: evidence connection and human applicability judgment. Missing evidence leaves an actual empty slot and a stationary clarification leaf; linking a reference moves the leaf only as far as a clearly open human-review gate. Review opens the original beside marked change and rationale, then files a condition-consistent clarification or draft. Combine T2's clause alignment, T4's preserved source layers, T1's evidence footprint, T3's physical withholding cue and T5's two-stage stop. Use one clause per phone panel, readable text outside the SVG, explicit state words plus shapes, and choice-specific announcements through the final artifact.

Build a clause review desk with a deliberate relay embedded in the document itself. Begin with a single enlarged T2 requirement/reply/evidence row, preserving T4 original and working-proof layers. A selected clause strip becomes the T5 baton; a T1 empty evidence footprint physically interrupts its path. When relevant evidence is linked, rework T3 feed/interlock into a restrained document-slot action that releases only an outlined draft, then stop separately at human applicability review. Missing evidence must remain a clarification in every later phase. Finish with original, change and rationale visible on the same review desk. This recombination keeps document comparison as TBE identity and borrows the relay causal logic without adopting the complete T5 scene or the entire press machine.

tbe.synthesis: A new documentary composition turns one operating-envelope requirement and vendor reply into a vertically registered clause folio. An empty or occupied evidence footprint controls a split paper interlock, while a separate human-review boundary stays unresolved. The selected state continues through a retained-original/working-proof spread and a common archival jacket. All five independent jury ballots and the aggregate informed the composition; Borda order is evidence of panel preference, not a winner-selection rule.
